name: North American T-6 / SNJ Texan
variants: Harvard II / IV (RAF/RCAF; Canadian Car & Foundry)
summary: WWII advanced trainer that trained most Allied fighter pilots; today the most common radial-engined warbird at US airshows and races.

wings: Low wing with a swept leading edge and straight trailing edge
Outer panels with dihedral and blunt, near-triangular tips
fuselage: Long framed greenhouse canopy over a tandem two-seat cockpit
Tailwheel gear; main wheels retract inward but stay partly visible
tail: Triangular, sharp-cornered fin and rudder (rounded on early versions)

tellTales: Radial-engined tandem trainer with a long framed greenhouse canopy
Taildragger with a triangular fin and rudder
Swept leading edge with a straight trailing edge

confusedWith.howToTell: The T-28 sits on tricycle gear and is bulkier; the Texan is a taildragger.
The modern Texan II is a turboprop with a long pointed nose, frameless bubble canopy and tricycle gear; the WWII Texan has a radial and a tailwheel.
The Mustang has a pointed inline-engine nose and a belly air scoop; the Texan has a round radial nose and a long framed two-seat canopy.
The Cornell has fixed gear, a light inline-style nose and a wire-free wing; the Texan is bigger with retractable gear and a big radial.
The BT-13 has fixed landing gear and a rounder, lower profile; the Texan has retractable gear and a taller canopy.
